check.help: Verify that the active profile's secrets resolve, without printing them
check.help_long:
Verify that the active profile's secrets resolve, without printing them

Validates the config, then resolves each secret that uses a provider and whose `if_missing` is `error`. References to unknown providers are reported as well. Values are never printed.

Secrets without a provider are not resolved. One with no default is reported only when its own `if_missing` is `error` or `warn`; `--if-missing` and `FNOX_IF_MISSING` do not apply to it, so an environment-only secret that is unset can still pass.

`--all` also resolves secrets whose `if_missing` is `warn` or `ignore`; their failures are reported as warnings, or not at all for `ignore`. Problems go to stderr, and fnox exits 1 when any error is found.
check.name: check

edit.help: Edit the config file, or one secret, with values decrypted
edit.help_long:
Edit the config file, or one secret, with values decrypted

Without KEY, decrypts or fetches every secret in the config file, across all profiles, into a private temporary copy and opens it in `$EDITOR` (then `$VISUAL`, then `vi`, or `notepad` on Windows). When the editor exits, fnox stores each new or changed value with its provider and writes the file back, keeping your comments and formatting. Unchanged values keep their existing ciphertext.

With KEY, only that secret's resolved value is written, raw and without TOML, to a private temporary file for the active profile. If you change it, fnox stores the new value with the secret's provider as `fnox set --from-file` does, keeping its other settings. The other secrets are not decrypted.

The editor command may include arguments, such as `EDITOR="code --wait"`. Secrets from read-only providers are shown but cannot be changed. fnox edits the file named by `-c` (default: `fnox.toml` in the current directory).
edit.name: edit

exec.help: Run a command with secrets in its environment
exec.help_long:
Run a command with secrets in its environment

Resolves the active profile's secrets and runs COMMAND with them set as environment variables. Secrets with `env = true` (the default) or `env = "exec"` are set; `env = false` secrets are not, and are removed if the parent environment has them. An `as_file` secret is written to a private temporary file whose path becomes the variable's value; the file is deleted when the command exits. Configured lease backends add short-lived credentials.

fnox also removes `FNOX_AGE_KEY`, `FNOX_AGE_KEY_FILE`, and the Enpass master password from the inherited environment, forwards Ctrl-C and `SIGTERM` to the command, and exits with the command's exit status. Put fnox options before `--`; everything after it is the command.

With `--redact` (or `redact_exec = true` / `FNOX_EXEC_REDACT=1`), secret values are replaced with `[REDACTED]` in the command's stdout and stderr, but only for a stream that is piped or redirected; a terminal is left untouched so interactive programs keep working. This is not a sandbox: a command can transform a value before printing it.
exec.name: exec
exec.after_help_long:
See also:
- Running commands: https://fnox.jdx.dev/guide/running-commands
- Profiles: https://fnox.jdx.dev/guide/profiles

export.help: Print or write resolved secrets as env, shell, JSON, YAML, or TOML
export.help_long:
Print or write resolved secrets as env, shell, JSON, YAML, or TOML

Resolves the active profile's secrets and prints them in the chosen format, or writes them to `--output`. By default only secrets with `env = true` are included, matching shell integration; `--all` adds `env = "exec"` and `env = false` secrets. An `as_file` secret is exported as the path of a temporary file that holds its value.

Name one or more KEYs to export only those secrets. Only the named secrets are resolved, so other secrets cost no provider calls or auth prompts. Naming a key includes it whatever its `env` setting, so `--all` is not needed. An unknown key is an error.

JSON, YAML, and TOML put the values in a `secrets` object, which `fnox import` reads back. The output contains real values, and `--output` creates the file with your default permissions, so set a restrictive umask first.
export.name: export

- Import and export: https://fnox.jdx.dev/guide/import-export

Write the files to their paths

Decrypts or fetches each file of the active profiles and writes it to the path that keys it, with mode `0600`, replacing whatever is there. A file whose content already matches is left alone. The content is written to a temporary file and renamed into place, so a symlink at the path is replaced, not followed. Every file is resolved before any is written.

With PATH arguments, only those files are written.

files.help_long:
Deploy files stored as secrets

A file is declared under `[files]` in the global config, keyed by the path it belongs at, and stored with the same providers as a secret. It is never an environment variable. Without a subcommand, `fnox files` lists them.

Store a file with `fnox set --file PATH`, change it with `fnox edit --file PATH`, print it with `fnox get --file PATH`, and write every file of the active profiles to its path with `fnox files write`.

import.help_long:
Encrypt secrets from a dotenv, JSON, YAML, or TOML file into the config

Reads key/value pairs from `--input` (or stdin), encrypts each value with the encryption provider named by `--provider`, and writes the ciphertext to the config file in the current directory, or to the global config with `--global`. Keys that already exist keep their other settings, such as `description` and `if_missing`. Remote storage providers cannot be import targets.

fnox lists the keys and asks for confirmation before writing. When the data comes from stdin, pass `--force` (or `--dry-run`), because stdin cannot also answer the prompt.

mcp.help: Serve secrets to AI agents over the Model Context Protocol
mcp.help_long:
Serve secrets to AI agents over the Model Context Protocol

Starts an MCP server on stdin and stdout for an agent client to launch. It offers the `get_secret` and `exec` tools, limited by the `[mcp]` table: `tools` chooses which tools are offered and `secrets` restricts which secrets they can reach. Add `request_secret` to `tools` to let the agent ask you to enter a missing secret on a local page. The server never prompts in the terminal, so authenticate to your providers before starting the client.

Inside `fnox proxy run` with `request_secret` enabled, the proxy serves the session instead: it offers only `request_secret` and injects each value the user enters into requests its rules allow.

run.help: Run a command with placeholder credentials behind the proxy
run.help_long:
Run a command with placeholder credentials behind the proxy

Resolves the secrets that `[[proxy.rules]]` names, plus any secrets their providers need, starts the proxy on a local port, and runs COMMAND with:

 - each rule's variable set to a placeholder instead of the real value
 - `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and `ALL_PROXY` pointing at the proxy, with
   a per-session password that other users' processes don't have
 - CA variables such as `SSL_CERT_FILE` pointing at the proxy's certificate
 - every configured secret and common cloud credential variables removed

With `--sandbox` (or `sandbox = true`), the command also runs in an OS sandbox: its only network route is the proxy, the filesystem is read-only except for the working directory and temporary files, and fnox's configuration, keys and common credential directories are hidden.

The command's HTTP client must honor those proxy and CA settings. fnox exits with the command's exit status.
run.name: run

Decrypts each matching secret stored with an encryption provider, such as age or a KMS, encrypts it again with that provider's current configuration, and writes the new ciphertext to the file that defines it. scan.help: Scan files for secrets committed in plaintext
scan.help_long:
Scan files for secrets committed in plaintext

Walks DIR and reports lines that look like cloud keys, API tokens, private keys, or password assignments, with the matched value redacted. It skips gitignored files, binary files, files over 5 MiB, and directories such as `.git`, `node_modules`, `target`, and `vendor`.

fnox exits 1 when it finds anything. Findings are heuristic: review each one, and do not treat a clean scan as proof that no secret is present.

With `--values`, fnox instead resolves the active profile's secrets and reports every file that contains one of their actual values. This has far fewer false positives than the pattern heuristics. Values are never printed, only the name of the matching secret. Empty secrets and secrets shorter than 8 characters are skipped. Add `--staged` to check the content staged in git (the index) rather than the working tree, and `--install-hook` to install a pre-commit hook that runs `fnox scan --values --staged`.

set.help: Store a secret and add it to the config
set.help_long:
Store a secret and add it to the config

Stores the value with a provider and records KEY in the config file in the current directory, or the global config with `--global`. With an encryption provider such as age, the ciphertext goes in the config. With a remote provider such as 1Password or AWS Secrets Manager, the value is written to the provider and the config records its key there. With no provider, the value is stored in plain text.

The provider is `--provider`, else the secret's current provider, else `default_provider`. When you omit VALUE, fnox reads piped stdin (trimming surrounding whitespace) or prompts with hidden input. `--from-file` reads a file verbatim, including trailing newlines. Passing only `--description`, `--default`, or `--if-missing` updates those settings without asking for a value.

sync.help: Cache remote secrets locally, encrypted with a local provider
sync.help_long:
Cache remote secrets locally, encrypted with a local provider

Fetches each secret whose provider differs from the target, encrypts the value with the target encryption provider, and stores the ciphertext in the secret's `sync` field. Later reads decrypt that copy instead of calling the source provider. The original reference stays in place, so run sync again after source values change.

The target is `--provider`, else `default_provider`, and must be an encryption provider. The cache is written to the `-c` file (default: `fnox.toml`), the global config with `--global`, or with `--local-file` a personal `fnox.local.toml` to keep out of git. A full `--local-file` sync also removes cache entries for secrets that no longer have a source.

age_key_file.help: Path to an age identity file for decrypting age secrets.
age_key_file.long_help:
Path to an age identity file for decrypting age secrets.

Used only when `FNOX_AGE_KEY` is unset and the age provider sets neither `identity` nor `key_file`; without it, fnox falls back to `age.txt` in the fnox config directory. Prefer `key_file` on the provider. The `--age-key-file` flag is deprecated and hidden, and overrides `FNOX_AGE_KEY_FILE` when both are set.

http_timeout.help: Timeout for HTTP requests that fnox makes itself.
http_timeout.long_help:
Timeout for HTTP requests that fnox makes itself.

Applies to lease backends such as Vault, GCP IAM, GitHub, and Cloudflare, to Lua plugin HTTP calls, and to the Azure App Configuration provider, so a slow server cannot hang `fnox exec`. Accepts a duration such as `30s`, `2m`, or `1h30m`. `0` disables the timeout; a value that does not parse means `30s`.

if_missing.help: What to do when any secret cannot be resolved, overriding the config.
if_missing.long_help:
What to do when any secret cannot be resolved, overriding the config.

`error` fails the command, `warn` prints a warning and continues, and `ignore` continues silently. This beats every `if_missing` in the config. The full order is: `--if-missing`, `FNOX_IF_MISSING`, the secret's `if_missing`, the top-level `if_missing`, `FNOX_IF_MISSING_DEFAULT`, then `warn`. An unknown value prints a warning and means `warn`.

if_missing_default.help: What to do when a secret cannot be resolved, if the config does not say.
if_missing_default.long_help:
What to do when a secret cannot be resolved, if the config does not say.

`error` fails the command, `warn` prints a warning and continues (the built-in default), and `ignore` continues silently. Unlike `FNOX_IF_MISSING`, it applies only to secrets with no `if_missing` in the secret or at the top level of the config. An unknown value prints a warning and means `warn`.

no_defaults.help: Use only the selected profile's secrets, without top-level `[secrets]`.
no_defaults.long_help:
Use only the selected profile's secrets, without top-level `[secrets]`.

By default a named profile inherits the top-level `[secrets]` table. With this set, only `[profiles.<name>.secrets]` (and the profile's own files) apply. `--no-defaults` overrides `FNOX_NO_DEFAULTS`.

profile.help: Profiles to use, separated by commas.
profile.long_help:
Profiles to use, separated by commas.

Selects which `[profiles.<name>]` tables and `fnox.<name>.toml` files apply. With several profiles, later ones override earlier ones. `--profile` overrides `FNOX_PROFILE`.

shell_integration_output.help: How much shell integration prints when it loads or unloads secrets.
shell_integration_output.long_help:
How much shell integration prints when it loads or unloads secrets.

`none` prints nothing, `normal` prints the keys that were loaded or unloaded, and `debug` also explains what the hook did, including why it exited early. `off`, `false`, and `0` also mean `none`; `verbose` also means `debug`. Any other value means `normal`.

about: Load secrets from encrypted files, password managers, and cloud secret stores
about_long:
Load secrets from encrypted files, password managers, and cloud secret stores

fnox reads `fnox.toml` from the current directory and its parents, resolves each secret through the provider it names, and hands the values to your shell or to the command you run.

Commands by task:

 - Read and run: get, list, exec, env, export, check
 - Store and migrate: set, remove, import, sync, reencrypt, edit, files
 - Configure: init, provider, plugin, profiles, config-files
 - Shell and tools: activate, deactivate, completion, tui, mcp
 - Diagnose: doctor, scan
 - Cache and broker: daemon, lease, proxy

Put fnox options before the `--` that starts a child command, as in `fnox -P prod exec -- npm start`. Everything after `--` belongs to the child command.
after_help_long:
See also:
- Quick start: https://fnox.jdx.dev/guide/quick-start
- Configuration reference: https://fnox.jdx.dev/reference/configuration
